newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat crop potential halved - consultant.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat crop potential halved - consultant.

text.p: Oklahoma may struggle to produce 100 million bushels of hard red winter wheat this year following recent freeze and disease damage, around half the total that might otherwise have been expected, private crop consultant Dale Fain said.
Fain said the crop potential in Kansas and Texas may also have been halved although he emphasized his information on those states was less extensive.
"It has been a big hit. I just think that every state is faced with that loss in potential of maybe half their crop," he said.
Fain, a former extension wheat specialist at Oklahoma State University, said travelling west from Enid, around 50 to 60 percent of the wheat plants had cell wall rupture.
"Wheat production that would have been 40 bushels (an acre) might now be around 20 to 25 bushels (in that part of the state)," he said.
In southwest Oklahoma, from Clinton through Hobart, he said cell wall ruptures were in the 50 to 70 percent range.
East of Enid, the level of cell wall rupture was lower, at maybe 20 to 30 percent, but disease problems were severe with septoria, tan spot and leaf rust widespread, Fain said.

"That in itself is going to curtail yields maybe as much as the freeze in that part of the state. You are going to see a downward pressure on yields of 20 to 30 percent just on disease (east of Enid), he said.
He noted leaf rust was also a serious problem in Texas.
